chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from one of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is appropriate for the Mutamatti' (one performing Umrah al-Mufradah followed by Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Tamattu') who has exited Ihram that he does not wear a shirt, and he should resemble the Muhrim (those in Ihram).
And whoever trims the hair of his head at the time of Ihram or combs it, it is not permissible for him except to shave (his head).
And whenever he limits himself to trimming (hair), a sheep's blood (dam) becomes obligatory upon him; he narrated that.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, then enters Ihram again for Hajj.
key_terms.اَلتَّقْصِيرُ: Trimming or cutting the hair, as opposed to shaving.
key_terms.اَلْإِحْرَامُ: The sacred state of consecration for pilgrimage, involving specific clothing and prohibitions.
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Sacrifice of a sheep, a form of expiation (fidyah) in Hajj.

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Mutamatti' pilgrim regarding clothing and hair after exiting Ihram for Umrah?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudence of Hajj, this hadith clarifies the transitional state of the Mutamatti', requiring him to maintain the spirit of Ihram by avoiding stitched garments and grooming acts like cutting or combing hair after Umrah. The stipulation of a sheep sacrifice (dam) for mere trimming highlights the severity of altering one's state prematurely, a ruling derived from the broader principles of Hajj rituals found in the Quran.
